- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3067-3072 (the if/elif block that resolves integration_ref_for_capture)
  Problem: The code comment at lines 3055-3062 documents "fail-open: if the fetch fails or the branch is unknown, the python heredoc skips the post-merge filter." But the implementation contradicts this contract. When `git fetch` fails and `git rev-parse --verify` succeeds on an existing local tracking ref, `integration_ref_for_capture` IS set to the stale local ref — the Python heredoc does NOT skip the filter. It proceeds, reading potentially wrong tree content via `git show <stale_ref>:<path>`. If a force-push happened on the remote, the filter checks old content and either keeps entries it should drop or (worse) drops entries it should keep because the stale tree still has the line.
  Why it fails at runtime: Suppose the integration branch gets force-pushed between capture ticks. The fetch fails (network hiccup, auth, etc.), the `elif` branch finds `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` exists locally at an old SHA, and `integration_ref_for_capture` is set. The Python heredoc runs `git show <old_sha>:<path>`, finds the line is still present in the pre-force-push tree, and drops the `must_not_contain` entry. But the real post-merge tree (post-force-push) no longer has that line — the entry should have survived. The verifier-side defense won't catch this because the entry was already dropped at capture time. Conversely, the filter could keep an entry that the real post-merge tree still contains, but the verifier would catch that case.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: 340-348 (`_find_pr_merge_commit_for_path`, the `git log -n 1` invocation)
  Problem: The function uses `git log -n 1 --format=%H --grep="#<pr_num>\b" -E <ref> -- <path>` which returns the most recent commit on `<ref>` whose message matches the PR number and that touched `<path>`. On an orchestator integration branch, the most recent matching commit may not be the sub-issue's squash-merge commit. If a later commit (e.g., a conflict resolver commit) mentions the same PR number and touches the same file, `-n 1` returns that later commit instead of the actual merge commit.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the later commit's version of the file re-introduced a line that the original PR genuinely removed, `_read_file_at_merge_commit` returns content where the pattern matches. The defense then classifies a genuine regression as a capture-side false positive, returns `satisfied=True`, and the gate passes despite the resolver having reverted the sub-issue's intent. The specific trigger requires: (a) a later commit on the integration branch that mentions the PR number, (b) touches the same file, and (c) re-introduces content the PR removed. This is low-probability but the mechanism is race-free — a resolver commit that says "Fixes regression from #2840" and touches the same file satisfies conditions (a) and (b); a resolver error that re-adds the deleted line satisfies (c).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
